raw.excerpt: About KasaKasa is the leading tech-enabled hotel and apartment hotel brand and manager.
raw.description:
About Kasa

Kasa is the leading tech-enabled hotel and apartment hotel brand and manager. We partner with owners of multifamily and boutique hospitality properties to deliver stylish, professionally managed accommodations to business and leisure travelers alike. We took the best that hotels and short-term rentals had to offer and created a new class of hospitality that is well-priced, reliable, and offers a large selection of great locations.

Unlike traditional hotel operators, we prioritize automation, AI-driven pricing, and data-driven decision-making to optimize revenue and improve guest experiences. Behind the scenes, we build technology that combines with our innovative operations to grow a globally scalable offering that delivers high-quality stays to guests. Our guests enjoy seamless check-ins, caring service, and attractive amenities — and if anything comes up, our on-site and remote guest experience team is available throughout their stay, ensuring our hospitality is rarely seen but always felt.

Role Overview

Kasa is seeking a People Program Manager to own a defined and evolving slate of People programs, including but not limited to performance scorecards, manager training and enablement, career tracks, the annual performance cycle, and engagement measurement. This role translates strategic organizational priorities into practical, well-run programs.

This role sits within Kasa’s People team and reports to the Director of People & Performance. It’s an individual contributor, program-ownership role: hands-on, analytically strong, and comfortable building repeatable systems end to end. This People Program Manager will work closely with our Senior People Business Partner, and the two roles are intended to work in close partnership with clear swim lanes. The priorities of this role are to:

  • Build programs that run without being chased. Own the systems behind how we evaluate, develop, and grow people, and use AI and automation to keep them repeatable and scalable.
  • Equip managers to lead well. Give our people managers the tools and training to coach their teams, give useful feedback, and grow talent.
  • Give leaders a clear view of team health. Turn People data into insights and recommendations that help us spot trends and retention risks early and act on them.

Key Responsibilities & Deliverables

Performance Scorecards & Manager Enablement

  • Build performance scorecards that give managers ongoing visibility into team health and impact
  • Design and run manager training and enablement programs that help managers set clear expectations, coach their teams, and grow as leaders
  • Build manager capability through training, resources, and job aids on the performance process

Career Tracks

  • Own the career tracks framework end-to-end, including leveling, competencies, and progression criteria across functions
  • Partner with functional leaders to define what good looks like at each level and keep tracks current as roles and the org evolve
  • Make progression transparent for employees through clear criteria, examples, and self-assessment tools so people know what's next and how to get there
  • Connect career tracks to performance, promotion, and compensation decisions so leveling stays consistent and defensible

Performance Review Cycle

  • Own the annual performance cycle end-to-end, including timeline, communications, calibration, and tooling
  • In partnership with key members of the People team, design the review process itself, including rating scales, self and peer input, and how performance connects to promotion and compensation decisions
  • Equip managers and employees with clear guidance, resources, and job aids so the process feels useful rather than administrative
  • Measure how the cycle lands through completion rates, quality of feedback, and manager and employee sentiment, then improve it each year

Engagement Measurement

  • Own our engagement measurement approach, including the engagement dashboard, as an early-detection system for retention risk
  • Turn engagement data into clear, actionable recommendations for leaders

Data Analysis & Reporting

  • Use People data and analytics to identify trends, track key metrics, and make data-driven recommendations
  • Translate quantitative and qualitative insights into concrete actions that improve the employee experience and business outcomes

Automations

  • Use AI tools to scale People programs, drafting and iterating on manager coaching materials and documentation templates that would otherwise take hours to produce manually
  • Build reusable, AI-assisted workflows for repetitive tasks so processes scale without added headcount. Examples include candidate tracking, employee onboarding, and benefits management

Success Metrics

More precise targets will be set with the Director, People & Performance in your first 90 days.

ThemeGeneral MetricsPerformance Scorecards & Manager Enablement

• 100% of managers and individual contributors using scorecards on a monthly or quarterly basis

• Higher team member satisfaction scores for training and enablement programs

Career Tracks• Career tracks established and routinely referenced for all job familiesPerformance Review Cycle• Our performance review process is fair, efficient, and useful in helping our team members grow and stay engagedEngagement Measurement• Engagement dashboard live and routinely used to understand engagement and retention risks across rolesRetention• Reduction in voluntary attrition (trailing 12mos), driven by manager training, career tracks, and engagement insightsData Analysis & Reporting• People data report (monthly or quarterly) delivered on scheduleAutomations• Measurable hours saved each month through reusable, AI-assisted workflows

Qualifications

Skills, Experience, & Expertise

  • Bilingual in English and Spanish
  • 3-5 years of HR generalist and/or program management experience, with a track record of owning programs end-to-end
  • Experience building performance/engagement scorecards or People Analytics dashboards, and comfort partnering with Programs and Data teams
  • Experience in a high-growth, distributed, or tech-enabled environment is a strong plus
  • Experience with core People systems: HRIS, performance management platform, and engagement survey tools, and comfort working across multiple People tech tools.

How You Work

  • You're a reliable and highly accountable owner, and you know how to take a program from a concept to a repeatable system, without needing to be chased
  • You communicate with clarity and empathy, whether you're training a room of managers or writing a policy document
  • You build systems and processes that outlast your involvement: repeatable, documented, and scalable
  • You're deeply curious about the employee experience and proactive about improving it
  • You flex easily across program work and generalist support as priorities shift
  • You see AI as leverage, not a threat to the human side of the job, and you use it to move faster on repeatable work so you have more time for the judgment calls and conversations that need a person
  • You have genuine interest in modernizing traditionally manual People workflows, consistent with Kasa's broader operating philosophy

Why This Role Is Different

You will have real ownership over the programs that give Kasa's leaders visibility into team health and the tools to lead well - performance scorecards, manager training, engagement measurement, and more. You will build and measure the infrastructure our People team has been wanting to invest in, with real autonomy over how you run it and a team that values your perspective.

Curious about the Kasa experience? Save when you book on !

Benefits

  • Remote Work: With flexibility as a core value, and over three-quarters of the team working remotely, Kasa employees can work from anywhere, including our Kasa’s across the country!
  • Kasa Travel Credit: We love to travel! Kasa employees get an allowance of free stays with us in any of our locations, plus a discount on any night for friends and family.
  • The Pay: The starting base pay range for this role is between $76,000 and $85,000 and is set based on multiple considerations, including business needs, market demands, talent availability, experience, and unique skills and attributes. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified. This role may also be eligible for equity, bonus, perks, benefits, and Kasa Travel Credits.
  • Generous Stock Option Plan: At Kasa, our compensation philosophy is to offer a total compensation package that over-indexes on equity to encourage our team to think like owners (by being owners) and benefit from the value growth that our collective hard work creates.
  • Flexible PTO: Full-time exempt Kasa employees are encouraged to take time off as they need and see fit, ensuring that it’s not disruptive to their work.
  • 401(k) Plan: As you invest in yourself and your future, Kasa invests in you too.
  • Health Coverage: We’ve invested in comprehensive health insurance options to help when you need it most.
  • Other Perks: Qualifying full-time roles are eligible for a wi-fi stipend, cell-phone reimbursement, home office stipend, and more!

Kasa is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by law. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

Kasa is an E-Verify participant. We will verify the identity and employment eligibility of all persons hired to work in the United States by matching information employees provide on the Form I-9 against records available to the Social Security Administration (SSA) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). You may find more information here and here.

Kasa does not accept unsolicited resumes from individual recruiters or third party recruiting agencies in response to job postings. No fee will be paid to third parties who submit unsolicited candidates directly to our hiring managers or People & Talent team.

A Note on Recruiting & Job Scams

The Kasa Talent Acquisition team will only communicate from email addresses that use the URLs and . We will not use apps such as Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, or Google Hangouts for communicating with you. We will never ask you to send us money or technology to work for our company. If you believe you are a scam victim, please review your local government consumer protections guidance and reach out to them directly. US-based applicants may refer to this article from consumer.ftc.gov for more details.

raw.excerpt: Als Digital Sales Engineer (m/w/d) bist Du im Homeoffice für die Betreuung und den Ausbau eines definierten Vertriebsgebiets verantwortlich.
raw.description:
Als Digital Sales Engineer (m/w/d) bist Du im Homeoffice für die Betreuung und den Ausbau eines definierten Vertriebsgebiets verantwortlich. Mit Hilfe digitaler Vertriebswerkzeuge identifizierst Du neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten, gewinnst Neukunden und pflegst langfristige Beziehungen zu Bestandskunden. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit europäischen Vertriebsteams setzt Du gezielte Kampagnen um, präsentierst innovative Lösungen und überzeugst Kunden von deren Mehrwert. Dabei zeichnen Dich Deine ausgeprägte Hunter-Mentalität, Deine Kommunikationsstärke sowie Dein Interesse an Technologie und Vertrieb aus. Wir freuen uns auf Deine Bewerbung!

In dieser Rolle bist Du für folgende Aufgaben verantwortlich:

  • Du bist verantwortlich für die Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Vertriebsstrategien, um nachhaltiges Umsatzwachstum in Deinem Vertriebsgebiet zu erzielen.

  • Du identifizierst und gewinnst neue Kunden durch den gezielten Einsatz digitaler Vertriebskanäle und baust langfristige Geschäftsbeziehungen auf.

  • Du betreust bestehende Kunden, erkennst deren Anforderungen frühzeitig und entwickelst passgenaue Lösungen zur Ausschöpfung weiterer Geschäftspotenziale.

  • Du planst und führst Vertriebs- und Marketingkampagnen in enger Zusammenarbeit mit europäischen Vertriebsteams durch, um die Marktpräsenz auszubauen.

  • Du setzt Dein technisches und kommerzielles Verständnis ein, um Kunden kompetent zu Produkten, Anwendungen und Lösungen zu beraten.

  • Du analysierst Vertriebskennzahlen, Marktpotenziale und Kundenbedarfe, um neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu identifizieren und den Vertriebserfolg nachhaltig zu steigern.

Dein Profil:

Du erkennst Chancen und Entwicklungen frühzeitig und setzt diese gezielt ein, um nachhaltige Verbesserungen zu erzielen. Bei deiner Arbeit orientierst du dich an den Anforderungen des Unternehmens sowie an den Bedürfnissen der verschiedenen Interessengruppen. Du kommunizierst klar, strukturiert und zielgerichtet und schaffst es, andere für gemeinsame Ziele zu begeistern. Durch deine offene und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise förderst du die Zusammenarbeit im Team und bringst unterschiedliche Perspektiven erfolgreich zusammen. Du handelst verantwortungsbewusst, denkst vorausschauend und leistest einen wertvollen Beitrag zur Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen, Strukturen und Beziehungen.

Für diese Rolle benötigst Du:

  • Technische Ausbildung oder Studium mit technischem Hintergrund erforderlich.

  • Mindestens drei Jahre nachweisbare Vertriebserfahrung.

  • Interesse an der Neukundenakquise sowie der Identifikation und Entwicklung neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten.

  • Ausgeprägte Kundenorientierung sowie die Fähigkeit, nachhaltige Kundenbeziehungen aufzubauen und zu pflegen.

  • Strukturierte und eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise sowie ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative.

  • Erfahrung in einem technischen oder technologiegetriebenen Umfeld.

  • Sehr gute Englisch-, Französisch- und Deutschkenntnisse.

Bevorzugte Qualifikationen, die dich auszeichnen:

  • Hohe Resilienz und die Fähigkeit, auch in herausfordernden Situationen professionell und zielorientiert zu agieren.

  • Lernbereitschaft, Anpassungsfähigkeit und Interesse an neuen Technologien und Vertriebsansätzen.

Unsere Kultur & unser Versprechen an dich:

Bei Emerson legen wir Wert auf einen Arbeitsplatz, an dem jede/r Mitarbeiter/in geschätzt und respektiert wird und an dem er/sie sich weiterentwickeln kann. Wir fördern ein Umfeld, das Innovation, Zusammenarbeit und unterschiedliche Perspektiven begünstigt - denn wir wissen, dass großartige Ideen von großartigen Teams kommen. Unser Engagement für eine kontinuierliche Karriereentwicklung und die Förderung einer integrativen Kultur stellt sicher, dass Du die Unterstützung erhältst, die Du benötigst, um erfolgreich zu sein. Ob durch Mentoring, Schulungen oder Führungsmöglichkeiten - wir investieren in Deinen Erfolg, damit Du einen nachhaltigen Beitrag leisten kannst. Wir sind davon überzeugt, dass vielfältige Teams, die zusammenarbeiten, der Schlüssel zum Wachstum und zur Erreichung von Geschäftsergebnissen sind.

Wir wissen, wie wichtig das Wohlbefinden unserer Mitarbeiter/innen ist. Wir legen Wert auf Zusammenarbeit und Teamwork und sorgen dafür, dass sich unsere Mitarbeiter/innen in allen Bereichen des Lebens unterstützt fühlen. Als Arbeitgeber glauben wir daran, dass man gemeinsam durchs Leben gehen kann - wir feiern die schönen Momente und geben Kraft in schwierigen Zeiten. Wir sind da, um die Meilensteine des Lebens mit finanzieller Unterstützung zu begleiten - sei es die Aufnahme eines neuen Familienmitglieds, eine Weiterbildung oder eine Heirat - und um eine helfende Hand zu reichen, wenn es schwierig wird, durch zusätzlichen Urlaub, Versicherungsschutz und aufmerksame Gesten. Unsere Leistungen gehen über das Wesentliche hinaus – wir bieten Lohnfortzahlung im Krankheitsfall, Fahrradleasing und psychologische Unterstützung durch unser Employee Assistance Program, das durch lokale Mental Health First Aider ergänzt wird. Um unser Team bei Kräften zu halten, bieten wir außerdem eine hauseigene Kantine, frisches Obst und eine Auswahl an kostenlosen Getränken.

raw.description:
Calling all originals: At Levi Strauss & Co., you can be yourself and be part of something bigger. We are a company of people who like to forge our own path and leave the world better than we found it. Who believe that what makes us different makes us stronger. So add your voice. Make an impact. Find your fit and your future.


Introduction

As an Engineering Manager within Systems Reliability Engineering, you will lead the engineering, modernization, and automation of the technology platforms that power Levi Strauss & Co. retail stores worldwide. You will guide a team of Store Platform Engineers while partnering across Retail Operations, Product, Infrastructure, Security, and Reliability Engineering to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure store technology solutions. This role reports to the Senior Manager, SRE & Platform Engineering.


About the Job

  • Lead and develop a high-performing Store Platform Engineering team, driving engineering excellence, mentoring talent, and supporting business priorities.
  • Define and execute the roadmap for store technology platforms, including endpoint management, device lifecycle management, platform modernization, and global technology standards.
  • Drive automation, self-service, and AI-enabled solutions that improve operational efficiency, scalability, and support experiences across the retail environment.
  • Partner with business and technology stakeholders to deliver secure, reliable, and intuitive technology platforms that support store associates and customer experiences globally.
  • Establish engineering governance, vendor management practices, and platform standards that improve reliability, consistency, and long-term operational performance.

  • Experience leading and developing technical engineering teams in large-scale, distributed environments.
  • Strong expertise in endpoint management, device lifecycle management, and retail technology platforms.
  • Experience delivering automation, self-service, platform modernization, and technology standardization initiatives.

At RYZE, we believe daily rituals create the foundation for living your greatest life. WHAT YOU'LL DO 🎯

We’re looking for an experienced, people-focused Customer Service Manager to lead and continuously improve RYZE’s global customer experience. In this role, you’ll oversee day-to-day contact center operations, develop high-performing teams, and use data and customer insights to improve service quality, efficiency, and consistency.


You’ll work closely with internal teams and external partners to address customer pain points, strengthen operational processes, and ensure every interaction reflects RYZE’s commitment to empathy, quality, and care. The ideal candidate is a confident people leader who can balance coaching, performance management, and strategic problem-solving in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Responsibilities will include:

raw.description:
Company Overview

Our client is a marketing team that works inside businesses with many locations, such as senior living communities, med spas, dental and healthcare groups, cannabis retailers, and schools. Its clients are in the US and Canada, and they pay a flat fee instead of a percentage of ad spend.

The company runs on Claude and has built its own operating system and client portal. AI agents do most of the production, so a small team can run a lot of client work.

Your Role

As Account Director, you're the final decision-maker on 6 to 10 client accounts, across paid media, websites, CRM, and creative. Agents and teammates bring you options, and you pick one, approve it, or send it back with the exact fix.

You report to the CEO and work as a peer to the founders. You'll start by taking over the approval queue on every active account. By day 90, delivery runs without the CEO in the loop, and you've built the tool or process that lets the team take on 5 more accounts with the same people.

Part of the job is building. You'll release features to the internal platform by directing Claude Code: you write the spec, test it on staging, and merge it. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to know exactly what you want and check that you got it.

This isn't an account manager role. If you've mostly passed the calls on spend, creative, or pricing to someone else, or you'd rather delegate to a team of specialists, it probably isn't the right fit.

You'll

  • Run the client relationship with owners, executive directors, and sales teams

  • Approve Google Ads and Meta builds before launch

  • Adjust budgets and bids, and cut the search terms that bring no leads

  • Own conversion tracking across GTM, GA4, and offline imports from the CRM

  • Direct WordPress rebuilds, then own go-live, redirects, and Search Console

  • Connect CRMs, call tracking, and forms so each lead can be followed to the sale

  • Approve client pricing changes, promotions, and policy pages

  • Sign off on weekly and monthly client reports before they go out

You Bring

  • 7+ years running marketing or growth for clients or at an agency

  • Final say on a client's ad spend, creative, or pricing, and you can name the decision

  • Google Ads and Meta campaigns you built and managed yourself

  • Daily work with Claude or a similar tool, and something real you released through it, like a site, an ad build, an automation, or code

  • The habit of checking AI output before it goes live

  • Comfort with tag managers, CRMs, DNS, and webhooks

  • Near-native English, and confidence saying no to a client on a call

  • The drive to grow with the company as it takes on more accounts

Bonus Points

  • Marketing work in senior living, med spas, dental, healthcare, cannabis retail, or education

  • Experience with industry CRMs such as ALIS, Pagoda, or Dutchie

  • Advertiser verification, A2P 10DLC registration, or HIPAA and cannabis ad rules handled yourself

  • WordPress beyond the editor, like themes, plugins, or a staging-to-production deploy

  • SQL, GitHub pull requests, or Supabase

What's Offered

  • Fully remote, full-time contractor role from LATAM

  • Working hours on US business hours

  • Paid in USD as a contractor. Share the range that fits your level and we'll go from there

  • Unlimited PTO, used responsibly, and you choose which holidays to take

  • A direct line to the CEO, with the founders as your peers

  • Room to grow as the company takes on more accounts

Interview Process

1️⃣ First Call: A 30-minute conversation with atomic✳HR
2️⃣ CEO Interview: The accounts you've run and the decisions that were yours
3️⃣ Co-founder Interview: How you'd work as a peer, and the final decision
4️⃣ Work Test: Possibly a short exercise, and you'll know how it's judged first

raw.description:
Présentation de l’organisation

Fondée en 1952, la Fondation des maladies du cœur et de l’AVC du Canada (Cœur + AVC) est un organisme de bienfaisance canadien voué à la prévention des maladies du cœur et de l’AVC, à la sauvegarde de vies et à l’amélioration du rétablissement des personnes touchées par ces maladies. Par le financement de la recherche, la sensibilisation du public, la défense des intérêts et le développement de partenariats, l’organisme contribue à faire progresser la santé cardiovasculaire et cérébrale et à améliorer la santé de la population canadienne.

Cœur + AVC soutient la recherche scientifique et l’innovation médicale afin de faire avancer la prévention, le diagnostic, le traitement et le rétablissement des personnes atteintes de maladies du cœur ou ayant subi un AVC. L’organisme travaille également à sensibiliser la population aux facteurs de risque, à encourager l’adoption de saines habitudes de vie, à améliorer l’accès à des soins rapides et efficaces et à promouvoir des politiques publiques favorables à la santé. Pour réaliser sa mission, il mobilise des chercheurs, des professionnels de la santé, des décideurs publics, des organismes communautaires, des bénévoles, des donateurs et des personnes ayant une expérience vécue de ces maladies.

Présent à l’échelle nationale et engagé depuis plus de 70 ans dans le soutien à la recherche médicale, Cœur + AVC a contribué à d’importantes avancées dans la prévention et le traitement des maladies cardiovasculaires et de l’AVC. Depuis sa création, l’organisme a investi plus de 1,7 milliard de dollars dans la recherche sur les maladies du cœur et l’AVC, grâce à la générosité de ses donateurs et à la mobilisation des communautés partout au Canada.

Cœur + AVC se distingue par :

  • Plus de 70 ans d’expérience consacrés à l’avancement de la santé cardiovasculaire et cérébrale par la recherche, l’éducation, la défense des intérêts et la sensibilisation du public.

  • Des investissements majeurs dans la recherche médicale qui favorisent les découvertes scientifiques et contribuent à améliorer la prévention, le diagnostic, le traitement et le rétablissement des personnes touchées par les maladies du cœur et l’AVC.

  • Une mission d’envergure nationale visant à réduire les répercussions des maladies cardiovasculaires et de l’AVC et à améliorer la santé de la population canadienne.

  • Un vaste réseau de chercheurs, de professionnels de la santé, de partenaires communautaires, de bénévoles et de donateurs qui unissent leurs efforts autour d’objectifs communs en matière de santé.

  • Une volonté de transformer les découvertes scientifiques en solutions concrètes, de sensibiliser davantage la population, de contribuer à l’amélioration des systèmes de soins de santé et de réduire les obstacles à un accès équitable aux soins.

  • Une solide tradition philanthropique reposant sur les dons de particuliers et d’institutions, les campagnes de financement et le développement de relations durables avec les donateurs, qui permettent de soutenir les priorités de l’organisme en matière de recherche et d’amélioration de la santé.

Responsabilités

Relevant de la vice-présidence principale, Québec, la personne titulaire du poste de vice-président(e), philanthropie – Québec assurera la direction stratégique et la gestion du développement philanthropique à l’échelle de la province. Ce rôle combine la direction de l’équipe de développement du Québec et la gestion directe d’un portefeuille de donateurs majeurs et de donateurs potentiels, avec pour objectif d’obtenir des dons importants et de soutenir les priorités de la Fondation.

Cette personne contribuera également à l’élaboration de la stratégie organisationnelle de la Fondation et à sa performance régionale, à titre de membre de ses instances de haute direction. En étroite collaboration avec la vice-présidence principale, Québec, le conseil consultatif provincial du Québec, les bénévoles et les équipes internes, elle veillera à développer et à renforcer les relations avec les donateurs, à repérer de nouvelles occasions de financement et à favoriser la croissance des revenus philanthropiques

Planification stratégique et développement philanthropique

  • Élaborer des stratégies philanthropiques pluriannuelles alignées sur les priorités de la Fondation.

  • Participer à la préparation des budgets annuels liés aux dons majeurs et assurer le suivi des résultats financiers et des prévisions.

  • Développer un solide bassin de donateurs potentiels et de partenaires.

  • Repérer les occasions de collaboration entre les dons majeurs, les dons planifiés, les collectes communautaires, les intermédiaires et les événements organisés par des tiers.

  • Travailler avec les équipes régionales et nationales pour maximiser les occasions de financement.

  • Renforcer le rôle stratégique de la philanthropie au sein de l’organisation.

Dons majeurs et relations avec les donateurs

  • Gérer personnellement un portefeuille de donateurs majeurs et potentiels, de la sollicitation à la fidélisation, en collaboration avec la vice-présidence principale.

  • Concevoir des approches personnalisées selon les intérêts et les priorités des donateurs.

  • Préparer des propositions de financement adaptées avec les équipes internes.

  • Identifier et qualifier de nouveaux donateurs potentiels grâce à la recherche, aux réseaux professionnels et aux recommandations.

  • Collaborer avec les équipes de collecte communautaire et de dons planifiés pour développer de nouvelles possibilités de dons majeurs et de dons combinés.

  • Diriger les relations avec les grands donateurs francophones, particulièrement au Québec.

  • Négocier et conclure les ententes de dons, tout en assurant la reconnaissance et la fidélisation des donateurs.

Mobilisation du conseil consultatif provincial du Québec

  • Soutenir la vice-présidence principale dans la mobilisation du conseil consultatif pour les activités philanthropiques.

  • Encourager la participation des membres aux initiatives de philanthropie d’entreprise, de commandite et de dons individuels.

  • Entretenir des relations de confiance avec les membres du conseil.

  • Présenter régulièrement les résultats et les progrès de l’équipe de développement philanthropique.

  • Appuyer la vice-présidence principale et la présidence du conseil dans le recrutement et la planification de la relève.

Relations avec les donateurs, les partenaires et les parties prenantes

  • Identifier et qualifier de nouveaux donateurs et partenaires en collaboration avec les équipes de développement philanthropique.

  • Présenter la mission, les orientations stratégiques et les priorités de financement de la Fondation.

  • Mobiliser les chercheurs, les cliniciens et les experts internes pour élaborer des propositions de financement convaincantes et soutenir les rencontres avec les donateurs.

  • Définir les stratégies de sollicitation et orienter les démarches de l’équipe auprès des donateurs potentiels.

  • Coordonner les efforts de financement autour des priorités de la Fondation.

  • Élaborer et superviser le plan annuel de communication et de fidélisation des donateurs.

  • Maintenir des relations durables avec les donateurs, les bénévoles et les partenaires.

Gestion des opérations et efficacité des activités de financement

  • Participer à la qualification, à l’attribution et au suivi des donateurs potentiels afin de faire progresser les démarches de sollicitation.

  • Assurer la consignation des interactions avec les donateurs, les sympathisants et les bénévoles dans la base de données dans un délai de 48 heures.

  • Coordonner les renseignements nécessaires aux activités de développement philanthropique.

  • Maintenir une connaissance approfondie des priorités de financement de la Fondation.

  • Collaborer avec les équipes centrales à la recherche de donateurs, à la gestion de l’information, à la préparation des propositions et aux activités de fidélisation.

  • Veiller au respect des politiques, des procédures et des normes professionnelles de la Fondation.

  • Participer à la planification annuelle, au suivi budgétaire et à l’évaluation des résultats philanthropiques.

Leadership, développement des équipes et collaboration

  • Diriger l’équipe de développement philanthropique du Québec, définir les priorités et optimiser l’utilisation des ressources.

  • Accompagner les membres de l’équipe dans leur développement professionnel et établir des objectifs de rendement clairs.

  • Favoriser la collaboration entre les équipes et les différentes fonctions de l’organisation.

  • Veiller à ce que l’équipe maîtrise les programmes, les travaux de recherche et les priorités de la Fondation afin de les présenter efficacement aux donateurs.

  • Soutenir les bénévoles engagés dans les activités de financement.

  • Collaborer avec les ressources humaines au recrutement et au développement des talents.

  • Mettre son expertise philanthropique au service des collègues et des bénévoles.

  • Participer aux instances de haute direction et contribuer aux orientations stratégiques ainsi qu’à la performance régionale de la Fondation.

Profil recherchéz

Qualifications et expérience professionnelles

  • Diplôme universitaire.

  • Minimum de 10 ans d’expérience en collecte de fonds dans un environnement bilingue.

  • Succès démontré dans la sollicitation et l’obtention de dons majeurs de 100 000 $ et plus.

  • Expérience dans la gestion des relations avec les donateurs, de l’identification à la sollicitation et à la fidélisation.

  • Expérience en planification philanthropique, en élaboration de budgets et en suivi de la performance financière.

  • Expérience en recrutement, en formation et en mobilisation de bénévoles ou de professionnels de la collecte de fonds.

  • Expérience dans la direction d’une campagne de dons majeurs, un atout.

  • Excellente maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.

  • Certification CFRE et participation à une association professionnelle pertinente, des atouts.

  • Connaissance des codes d’éthique, des politiques et des procédures de l’AFP, de l’ACPDP (CAGP) et de l’APRA.

Compétences, connaissances et qualités recherchées

  • Vision stratégique et capacité à maintenir une vue d’ensemble tout en portant attention aux détails.

  • Solides compétences analytiques et aisance dans l’utilisation de plusieurs bases de données.

  • Capacité démontrée à développer des relations durables avec les donateurs et à obtenir des contributions philanthropiques majeures.

  • Excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles, relationnelles et en négociation.

  • Excellentes habiletés de communication, à l’oral comme à l’écrit, et expérience dans la rédaction de propositions de financement, de demandes de subvention, de lettres, de communications destinées aux donateurs et de documents d’information pour les bénévoles.

  • Capacité à collaborer efficacement avec les bénévoles, les membres du conseil, les donateurs et les équipes internes.

  • Leadership collaboratif et aptitude à mobiliser, accompagner et développer une équipe.

  • Capacité à concilier la planification stratégique, la gestion d’équipe et les relations directes avec les donateurs.

  • Engagement envers les normes d’éthique professionnelle en collecte de fonds et les bonnes pratiques de gestion et de fidélisation des donateurs.

Contexte du poste

Le poste de vice-président(e), philanthropie – Québec est un poste nouvellement créé, permanent et à temps plein, au sein du service du développement philanthropique. Relevant de la vice-présidence principale, Québec, la personne titulaire sera responsable du développement philanthropique à l’échelle de la province, tout en assurant personnellement la gestion d’un portefeuille de donateurs majeurs et de donateurs potentiels.

Cette fonction conjugue orientation stratégique, sollicitation de dons et gestion d’équipe. La personne titulaire travaillera en étroite collaboration avec la vice-présidence principale, le conseil consultatif provincial du Québec, les bénévoles et les différentes équipes de la Fondation afin de repérer de nouvelles possibilités de financement et de contribuer à la réalisation des priorités de l’organisation.

Les principales priorités consisteront à élargir le bassin de donateurs majeurs, à établir des relations durables avec les donateurs et les partenaires et à obtenir des contributions philanthropiques importantes. Le poste comporte un objectif annuel de 1 million de dollars en dons majeurs, accompagné de perspectives de croissance ambitieuses. La personne titulaire sera également responsable de la planification annuelle et du suivi financier des activités philanthropiques.

Le Groupe Mandrake mène ce processus de recrutement pour le compte de Cœur + AVC. Si cette occasion vous intéresse, veuillez envoyer votre lettre de présentation et votre CV par courriel à Alexandre Raymond, à l’adresse , en indiquant le titre du poste dans l’objet du courriel. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes retenues pour une entrevue seront contactées. Nous vous remercions de votre intérêt.

Organization Summary
Founded in 1952, Heart & Stroke is a Canadian health charity dedicated to preventing heart disease and stroke, saving lives, and improving recovery for people affected by these conditions. Through its research funding, public education, advocacy and partnerships, the organization works to advance cardiovascular and brain health and improve health outcomes across Canada.

Heart & Stroke supports scientific research and medical innovation aimed at improving the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and recovery of heart disease and stroke. It also works to raise public awareness of risk factors, promote healthier lifestyles, improve access to timely and effective care, and advocate for policies that support better health outcomes. Its work brings together researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, community organizations, volunteers, donors, and people with lived experience.

With a national presence and a long-standing commitment to medical research, Heart & Stroke has contributed to significant advances in cardiovascular and stroke care. Since its founding, the organization has invested more than $1.7 billion in heart disease and stroke research, supported by the generosity of donors and the engagement of communities across the country.

Heart & Stroke’s work is characterized by:
  • More than 70 years of experience advancing heart and brain health through research, education, advocacy, and public engagement.
  • A substantial investment in medical research to support scientific discoveries and improve the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and recovery of heart disease and stroke.
  • A national mission focused on reducing the impact of cardiovascular disease and stroke and improving health outcomes for Canadians.
  • A broad network of researchers, healthcare professionals, community partners, volunteers, and donors working toward shared health objectives.
  • A commitment to translating research into practical solutions, increasing public awareness, improving healthcare systems, and addressing barriers to equitable access to care.
  • A philanthropic foundation built on individual and institutional giving, fundraising initiatives and long-term donor relationships that help sustain its research and health-impact priorities.

Main Responsibilities
Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Quebec, the Vice President, Philanthropy – Quebec will provide strategic leadership and management for philanthropic development across the province. The role combines leadership of the Quebec Development team with direct responsibility for a portfolio of major donors and prospects, with a focus on securing significant gifts and supporting the Foundation’s priorities.

The Vice President will also contribute to the Foundation’s organizational strategy and regional performance as a member of its senior leadership groups. Working closely with the Senior Vice President, the Quebec Provincial Advisory Board, volunteers, and internal teams, the incumbent will develop donor relationships, identify new fundraising opportunities, and support the growth of philanthropic revenue.

Strategic Planning and Fundraising Growth

  • Develop philanthropic plans focused on multi-year giving and aligned with the Foundation’s strategic priorities.

  • Support the development of annual major gifts revenue and expense budgets and regularly review financial results and projections.

  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline of prospective donors and partners.

  • Identify opportunities for collaboration across major gifts, legacy giving, community fundraising, intermediary relationships, and third-party events.

  • Collaborate with colleagues across regions and functions to identify fundraising opportunities and strengthen collaboration.

  • Contribute to the development of philanthropy as a core organizational capability.

Major Gifts and Donor Relationships

  • Personally manage a portfolio of major donors and prospects, overseeing cultivation, solicitation, recognition, and stewardship in collaboration with the Senior Vice President.

  • Develop tailored approaches to donor engagement and solicitation based on individual interests and giving priorities.

  • Collaborate with internal teams to develop customized proposals and solicitations.

  • Identify and qualify new prospects through research, professional networks, staff, and volunteer referrals.

  • Collaborate with community fundraising colleagues to identify potential major gift donors.

  • Collaborate with legacy advisors to identify opportunities for blended gifts.

  • Lead relationships with French-speaking major donors, particularly in Quebec, in collaboration with the Senior Vice President.

  • Negotiate gift terms, bring solicitations to a close, and ensure appropriate donor recognition and stewardship.

Provincial Advisory Board Engagement

  • Support the Senior Vice President in engaging the Quebec Provincial Advisory Board in fundraising activities.

  • Engage board members in corporate philanthropy, sponsorships, and individual giving.

  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with board members.

  • Provide regular updates to the board on the Development team’s progress
  • Support the Senior Vice President and Board Chair with board recruitment and succession planning.

Donor, Partner, and Stakeholder Management

  • Identify, research, and qualify prospective donors and partners in collaboration with Development colleagues.

  • Communicate the Foundation’s mission, strategic plan, and funding priorities to donors and prospects.

  • Collaborate with internal teams, including scientists and clinicians, to develop compelling funding opportunities and ensure the appropriate expertise is represented in donor meetings and events.

  • Develop and prioritize cultivation and solicitation strategies for assigned prospects and provide direction to the Development team.

  • Coordinate fundraising approaches across teams in support of the Foundation’s highest-priority needs.

  • Develop and oversee an annual donor stewardship and communications plan.

  • Maintain strong relationships with donors, volunteers, and partners, ensuring appropriate recognition and ongoing stewardship.

Operations, Business Planning and Fundraising Effectiveness

  • Participate in prospect clearance and moves management processes to advance donor relationships.

  • Ensure that interactions with prospects, supporters, and volunteers are recorded in the database within 48 hours.

  • Coordinate information needed to support prospect development and fundraising activities.

  • Stay informed about the Foundation’s priority funding opportunities.

  • Collaborate with central Development teams on prospect research, information management, proposal development, donor communications, recognition, and stewardship.

  • Ensure compliance with the Foundation’s policies, procedures, Development standards, and professional conduct requirements.
  • Contribute to annual planning, financial oversight, and monitoring of fundraising performance.

Leadership, Team Development and Collaboration

  • Lead and develop the Quebec Development team, providing clear direction on priorities and ensuring resources are allocated effectively.

  • Coach and advise team members, support their professional development, and establish individual performance goals.

  • Foster strong working relationships across teams and functions.

  • Ensure Development staff can communicate effectively about the Foundation’s research, programs, and priorities.

  • Support volunteer groups involved in fundraising initiatives.

  • Work with Human Resources on recruitment and talent development.

  • Provide guidance and fundraising expertise to colleagues and volunteers.
    Contribute to organizational strategy and regional performance as a member of the Foundation’s senior leadership groups.

The Ideal Candidate Profile

Professional Qualifications and Experience

  • University degree.

  • At least 10 years of fundraising experience in a bilingual market.

  • Demonstrated success in soliciting and securing major gifts of $100,000 or more.

  • Experience managing donor relationships throughout the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship process.

  • Experience developing philanthropic plans and contributing to fundraising budgets and financial performance monitoring.

  • Experience recruiting, training, and collaborating with volunteers or fundraisers.

  • Experience leading a major gift campaign is an asset.

  • Full bilingual proficiency in French and English.

  • CFRE designation and involvement in a relevant professional association are assets.

  • Familiarity with the codes of ethics, policies, and procedures of AFP, CAGP, and APRA.

Desired Skills, Knowledge, and Attributes

  • Strategic thinker who can see the bigger picture while maintaining attention to detail.

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to work with multiple databases.

  • Proven ability to develop donor relationships and secure significant philanthropic contributions.

  • Excellent interpersonal, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.

Job Context

The Vice President, Philanthropy – Quebec is a newly created, full-time, permanent position within the Development department. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Quebec, the incumbent will lead philanthropic development across the province while personally managing a portfolio of major donors and prospects.

The role combines strategic leadership, hands-on fundraising, and team management. The Vice President will work closely with the Senior Vice President, the Quebec Provincial Advisory Board, volunteers, and colleagues across Development and other internal teams to identify fundraising opportunities and advance the Foundation’s priorities.

A key focus will be to strengthen the major gifts pipeline, develop relationships with donors and partners, and secure significant philanthropic contributions. The position has an annual major gifts revenue goal of $1 million, with high growth expectations, and includes responsibility for annual planning and financial oversight

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing proposals, grants, letters, donor communications, and volunteer briefings.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with volunteers, board members, donors, and internal stakeholders.

  • Collaborative leadership style, with the ability to coach and develop a team.

  • Ability to balance strategic planning and team leadership with direct donor engagement.

  • Commitment to professional fundraising ethics and responsible donor stewardship.

Mandrake Group is conducting this search on behalf of Heart & Stroke. If you are interested in this opportunity, please email your cover letter and CV to Alexandre Raymond at and include the job title in the subject line. Please note that only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you for your interest.

Job Summary

We are seeking an Experienced Corporate Counsel, M&A to serve as a critical strategic advisor to our executive leadership team and lead executioner for our corporate development initiatives. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), you will quarterback complex buy-side and sell-side transactions from inception to integration, directly safeguarding and expanding our multi-million dollar federal revenue portfolio.

In this high-impact, in-house role, you will be responsible for translating complex legal risks into clear, actionable business intelligence for members of the C-Suite, enabling data-driven, strategic decision-making. Operating at the intersection of corporate law and federal procurement, you will navigate the unique regulatory complexities of a Large Business federal contractor, including FAR/DFARS compliance, SBA affiliation risks, and contract novations. If you are a seasoned transactional attorney with a sharp business acumen and a proven track record of successfully executing GovCon deals, this role offers the platform to directly shape our growth strategy and corporate footprint.

As with any position, additional expectations exist. Some of these include, but are not limited to, adhering to normal working hours, meeting deadlines, following company policies as outlined by the Employee Handbook, communicating regularly with assigned supervisor(s), staying focused on the assigned tasks, and completing other tasks as assigned.

Job Description

Reporting Structure & Collaboration

  • Direct Report: Reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO).
  • Executive Advisory: Prepares and delivers comprehensive M&A transaction summaries, legal risk assessments, and financial exposure details to members of the C-Suite (COSS, COSD and CSO) for strategic decision-making purposes.

Main Duties

  • Transaction Execution: Lead internal deal teams through all phases of buy-side and sell-side GovCon transactions.
  • Contract Risk Mitigation: Review target companies' existing federal contract portfolios, evaluating Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) compliance, subcontracting plans, and active industrial security requirements.
  • Novation Strategy: Author, coordinate, and submit complex novation agreement packages to Administrative Contracting Officers (ACOs) to legally transfer acquired federal contracts without breaching anti-assignment statutes.
  • Internal Business Advisory: Partner directly with the Executive Team, Corporate Development, and Business Unit leads to assess the strategic fit and regulatory risks of potential acquisitions.
  • Outside Counsel Management: Direct and manage external law firms and specialized GovCon consultants to control legal spending and ensure transaction deadlines are met.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Deal Velocity & Efficiency: Time-to-close metrics on targeted acquisitions, ensuring legal milestones are met without causing project friction or deal fatigue.
  • C-Suite Reporting Accuracy: Quality, clarity, and timeliness of executive briefs and executive-level transaction risk matrices provided to the CEO and C-Suite.
  • Regulatory Compliance Post-Closing: Zero post-transaction compliance penalties or contract losses stemming from undisclosed FAR, DFARS, or SBA affiliation risks.
  • Novation Success Rate: Average time required to obtain signed novation agreements from federal Administrative Contracting Officers (ACOs) following a transaction closing.
  • Legal Budget Efficiency: Management of outside counsel spend relative to the established legal budget for each individual M&A transaction.

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Education: Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school.
  • Licensure: Active member in good standing with a state bar; eligible for local In-House Counsel Licensure if relocating.
  • Experience: 8 to 12+ years of corporate transactional experience, blending initial training at a major law firm ("BigLaw") with meaningful corporate in-house experience at a large federal contractor.
  • Core Knowledge: Advanced fluency in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Small Business Administration (SBA) size affiliation rules, Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), and organizational conflicts of interest (OCI).
  • Security Clearance: Ability to obtain or maintain an active U.S. Security Clearance (Secret or Top Secret) based on the company's classified contract pipeline.
  • If applicable: If you are or have been recently employed by the U.S. government, a post-employment ethics letter will be required if employment with VSolvit is offered

Company Summary

Join the VSolvit Team! Founded in 2006, VSolvit (pronounced 'We Solve It') is a technology services provider that specializes in cybersecurity, cloud computing, geographic information systems (GIS), business intelligence (BI) systems, data warehousing, engineering services, and custom database and application development. VSolvit is an award winning WOSB, CA CDB, MBE, WBE, and CMMI Level 3 certified company. We offer a customizable health benefits program that best meets the needs of its employees. Offering may include: medical, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, long and short-term disability and other insurance products, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Account, 401K Retirement Plan options, Tuition Reimbursement, and assorted voluntary benefits. Our goal is to grow together and enjoy the work that we do as a team.

VSolvit LLC is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Position Summary

As head of the Enterprise Project Management Office, you will lead the organization’s enterprise project, program, and portfolio management function at both strategic and operational levels. This role develops and matures PMO governance, standards, tools, reporting, and delivery practices to ensure enterprise initiatives are prioritized, executed, and measured in alignment with business strategy. Reporting to the Chief Transformation Officer, the Director of Enterprise PMO partners with executive leadership, business stakeholders, and delivery teams to improve portfolio visibility, strengthen delivery predictability, manage enterprise-level risks and dependencies, and build project management capability across the organization.

Hiring Range: $164,000-$214,000 annually, based on performance; this is a bonus-eligible position.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without restriction for any employer. We cannot provide visa sponsorship or assume existing sponsorships.

Key Responsibilities

  • Directs and manages the Enterprise PMO function, including project managers, program managers, analysts, coordinators, and related delivery resources.
  • Owns the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise project management methodologies, governance processes, standards, templates, and best practices.
  • Manages the enterprise project portfolio, ensuring initiatives align with organizational priorities, strategic goals, resource capacity, business value, and budget constraints.
  • Leads portfolio intake, prioritization, approval, and stage-gate review processes in partnership with the Chief Transformation Officer, executive leadership, and business leaders.
  • Prepares and presents executive-level reporting on portfolio health, project performance, transformation progress, risks, issues, dependencies, budgets, timelines, benefits realization, and resource utilization.
  • Partners with business leaders, IT, finance, procurement, operations, human resources, legal, compliance, vendors, and other stakeholders to translate strategic objectives into actionable programs and projects.
  • Drives accountability for delivery outcomes, including scope, schedule, budget, quality, benefits realization, adoption, and stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Identifies and manages portfolio-level risks, resource constraints, delivery conflicts, and cross-functional dependencies; escalates and resolves issues through appropriate governance channels.
  • Develops and maintains standardized project documentation, dashboards, roadmaps, portfolio metrics, lessons learned, and governance materials.
  • Leads PMO tool strategy and adoption, including project planning, reporting, collaboration, capacity planning, and portfolio management platforms.
  • Coaches, mentors, and develops project management staff; establishes clear performance expectations and promotes a culture of transparency, accountability, continuous improvement, and delivery excellence.
  • Supports organizational change management by ensuring projects include appropriate communication, training, stakeholder engagement, adoption, and transition plans.
  • Ensures project delivery practices comply with internal controls, audit requirements, risk management standards, procurement processes, and financial governance expectations.

Job Title: Data Entry Specialist

Job Type: (Remote)

Job Summary

The Data Entry Specialist — Finance & Accounting is responsible for accurately entering, verifying, processing, and maintaining financial and accounting information in company systems. This position supports Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, billing, expense management, reconciliations, and financial reporting by ensuring financial data and supporting documentation are complete, accurate, and properly recorded.

Key Responsibilities

  • Enter financial transactions accurately into ERP, accounting, and financial management systems.

  • Process invoices, purchase orders, receipts, payment records, expense reports, credit memos, and other financial documents.

  • Review source documents and verify transaction details before entering financial information.

  • Validate vendor, customer, account, amount, date, tax, payment-term, and coding information.

  • Perform data entry for Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, billing, and other accounting transactions.

  • Maintain accurate vendor, customer, account, and financial master data.

  • Assist with invoice processing and matching invoices with purchase orders and supporting documentation.

  • Enter and update payment, receipt, credit, debit, and adjustment information.

  • Assist with General Ledger transaction entry and supporting documentation.

  • Support journal-entry preparation and data gathering under the direction of accounting personnel.

  • Perform financial data validation and identify duplicate, missing, or inconsistent transactions.

  • Assist with account reconciliations by comparing system records with invoices, statements, receipts, and other source documents.

  • Maintain accurate records of invoices, payments, receipts, expenses, credits, adjustments, and other financial transactions.

  • Support employee expense and reimbursement processing.

  • Assist with customer billing and account updates as required.

  • Prepare spreadsheets, transaction reports, financial schedules, and other accounting documentation.

  • Support month-end, quarter-end, and year-end closing activities by providing accurate transaction data and documentation.

  • Research and correct data-entry errors and accounting discrepancies.

  • Scan, upload, organize, and electronically archive financial documents.

  • Maintain complete audit trails and supporting documentation for financial transactions.

  • Retrieve financial records and transaction details for authorized accounting personnel and auditors.

  • Assist with financial data cleanup, database maintenance, and record updates.

  • Maintain confidentiality of financial, customer, vendor, employee, and company information.

  • Follow accounting policies, internal controls, approval procedures, and document-retention requirements.

  • Meet established accuracy, productivity, processing, and reporting deadlines.

  • Identify opportunities to improve accounting data-entry processes, reduce errors, and increase efficiency.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Associate or bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

  • 1–3 years of experience in accounting data entry, finance, accounts payable, accounts receivable, bookkeeping, or related administrative work.

  • Strong numerical and data-entry skills with a high level of accuracy.

  • Basic understanding of accounting principles and financial terminology.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook.

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

  • Ability to process high volumes of financial transactions accurately.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive financial information.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ERP and accounting systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics, or similar platforms.

  • Experience processing invoices, purchase orders, payments, receipts, expense reports, and financial adjustments.

  • Knowledge of Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and General Ledger processes.

  • Experience with account and bank reconciliations.

  • Experience with automated invoice-processing or document-management systems.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, sorting, filtering, pivot tables, and data validation.

  • Familiarity with internal controls and audit documentation.

  • Experience supporting month-end and year-end close.

  • Knowledge of financial reporting and accounting documentation requirements.

Key Skills

  • Finance & Accounting

  • Financial Data Entry

  • Accounts Payable

  • Accounts Receivable

  • General Ledger Support

  • Invoice Processing

  • Payment Processing

  • Expense Processing

  • Financial Data Validation

  • Account Reconciliation

  • Vendor & Customer Records

  • ERP / Accounting Systems

  • Microsoft Excel

  • Data Verification

  • Transaction Processing

  • Financial Records Management

  • Document Management

  • Audit Support

  • Data Accuracy

  • Internal Controls

  • Confidentiality

  • Reporting Support

Core Competencies

  • Financial Data Accuracy: Ability to enter, verify, and maintain financial transactions with a high degree of accuracy.

  • Accounting Knowledge: Understanding of invoices, payments, expenses, accounts payable, accounts receivable, general ledger transactions, and financial documentation.

  • Attention to Detail: Ability to identify discrepancies, duplicate transactions, missing information, and incorrect accounting data.

  • Data Validation: Ability to compare system information against source documents and ensure financial records are complete and reliable.

  • Reconciliation Support: Ability to assist with comparing financial records and investigating differences.

  • Organization: Ability to maintain accurate financial records, spreadsheets, files, and supporting documentation.

  • Confidentiality: Ability to protect sensitive financial, employee, customer, and vendor information.

  • Process Compliance: Ability to follow accounting policies, internal controls, approval workflows, and documentation procedures.

  • Time Management: Ability to process high volumes of financial data while meeting established deadlines.

  • Problem Solving: Ability to investigate data and transaction discrepancies and coordinate corrections with accounting personnel.

  • Technology Proficiency: Ability to efficiently use ERP systems, accounting software, spreadsheets, databases, and document-management tools.

Overview

Lifeway is seeking a Remote Paid Media Strategist to take hands-on ownership of Google Ads, YouTube, and Bing / Microsoft Advertising as we bring paid media management in-house. You'll plan, build, optimize, and measure campaigns (search, Performance Max, video, audience-driven and Demand Gen) that drive customer acquisition, lead generation, eCommerce revenue, and ministry reach. You'll serve as the platform expert and trusted advisor to ministry and business partners while stewarding media budgets as entrusted funds. This is a remote-eligible role with periodic travel to Nashville for team gatherings.

Why Lifeway?

Lifeway is a place where you can bring your faith and work experience to join in the most important mission in the world: making disciples of Jesus Christ. Whether you’re a creator or storyteller, data guru or problem-solver, or anywhere in between, if you’re passionate about serving the church, we have a place for you. Lifeway has a strong Work from Anywhere (WFA) culture that is deeply focused on our mission and values. While headquartered in Nashville, TN, many of our positions are remote-eligible and have autonomy and flexibility with work hours. We provide equipment and resources to ensure team members have access to a productive and ergonomic workspace. We believe building relationships and community is essential to how we work together, so Lifeway hosts all-team meetings several times per year and provides travel for key team gatherings for remote-based team members. Full-time employees are eligible for enrollment in our comprehensive benefits plans including healthcare, vacation and sick time, holiday pay, care days, 401(k) plan, maternity and parental leave, adoption assistance, mission trip time, and more. If this sounds like a place where you would be excited to serve the kingdom of God, we would love for you to join our team.

Learn more about our culture at team.lifeway.com/culture-code

This is a remote position in the U.S. with occasional travel to Nashville for in-person team gatherings.

Responsibilities

  • Lives out Lifeway’s mission and values, showing deep commitment to Kingdom work
  • Own strategy, structure, and best practices for Google Ads, YouTube, and Microsoft Advertising, including search, Performance Max, video, shopping, and Demand Gen.
  • Turn ministry and business goals into channel media plans covering audiences, bidding, budget allocation, flighting, and measurement.
  • Build, traffic, and quality-check campaigns, ad groups, audiences, and creative variations before launch.
  • Manage and pace platform budgets, forecast spend, and recommend reallocations to Paid Media leadership and partners.
  • Run a structured testing roadmap (A/B and incrementality), documenting hypotheses, results, and what you learned.
  • Build dashboards and recurring reports, and explain performance in plain terms, including when results miss goals, with recommended next steps.
  • Manage audiences, first-party data uploads, exclusions, conversion tracking, and UTM structures in line with platform policy, privacy rules, and Lifeway standards.
  • Advise cross-functional teams, and other partners on what the channel can realistically deliver.
  • Define creative requirements and brief Creative based on performance evidence.
  • Work with platform reps and vendor partners, pursue certifications and betas, and share what you learn across the marketing team.
  • Limited travel: 2-4 times per year to Nashville, typically for 2-3 days

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Advertising, Communications, Analytics, or a related field, required

Master's degree, preferred

Advanced graduate degree (PhD, etc.), not required

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, required

  • 5+ years of hands-on paid media experience managing campaigns directly in platform interfaces, in-house or agency
  • Demonstrated depth in Google and Bing ad platforms, including campaign structure, bidding, audience strategy, and troubleshooting
  • Proven management and pacing of media budgets against CPA/CPL, ROAS, revenue, or lead goals
  • Working proficiency with GA4, pixels/Conversions API, UTMs, and attribution concepts
  • Experience designing and running structured A/B tests and applying the results
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including explaining performance to non-technical audiences
  • Ability to manage multiple campaigns and stakeholders with sound judgment and accuracy
  • Ability to travel to the Middle Tennessee area 2-4 times annually for team gatherings

Actively involved in an evangelical Christian church

Skills, Knowledge, & Experiences, preferred

  • Google Ads, Google Analytics, or comparable platform certification
  • Microsoft Bing Advertising certification
  • Experience managing paid media for multiple brands, audiences, or business units
  • Experience with Data Studio, Tableau, Power BI, Supermetrics, or similar reporting tools
  • Familiarity with incrementality testing, media mix modeling, or multi-touch attribution
  • eCommerce or direct-response experience (shopping campaigns, product feeds)
  • Experience in publishing, retail, ministry/nonprofit, or a multi-brand organization

raw.description:
Department Overview

The C3 Patient Access Resource Staff is responsible for providing the highest level of customer service while handling all aspects of the scheduling of clinic appointments, referral management, visit preparation, patient eligibility, and financial clearance for the Connected Care Center clinical services. This position is responsible for all aspects of scheduling and supporting patient care coordination across multiple clinical specialties. This position will respond to patient Connected Care Center scheduling requests which include but are not limited to, patient phone calls, MyChart or provider requests. The employee in this position promotes OHSU¿s mission statement by delivering high quality, cost effective, patient centered, service excellence.

Function/Duties of Position

Customer Service

  • Deliver exceptional customer service to external customers (patients, families, referring providers, insurance carriers, etc.) and internal customers (OHSU healthcare providers and staff).
  • Meet or exceed service standards of the healthcare industry.
  • Communicate promptly and professionally.
  • Demonstrate patient-centered customer service skills.
  • Handle crisis situations effectively.
  • Utilize available information technology efficiently.
  • Process complaints following standard procedures.
  • Provide flexible coverage for internal service needs.

Multi-Specialty Call Processing & Scheduling

  • Answer incoming calls and handle various inquiries related to scheduling, general information, referral status, and care-related matters.
  • Transfer calls to Nurse Triage when necessary, following established guidelines.
  • Schedule and manage patient access to clinical services in the Connected Care Center.
  • Record accurate and detailed information in the electronic medical record (EMR) for telephone encounters, including medication refill requests, complaints, general inquiries, and urgent healthcare concerns.
  • Assess and direct calls to the appropriate staff for patient care and needs.
  • Process calls promptly, professionally, and courteously.
  • Provide callers with relevant information, such as directions, addresses, and operating hours.
  • Utilize schedules and departmental procedures to connect callers with the appropriate on-call personnel.
  • Follow departmental policies for different types of encounters (e.g., refills, telephone consultations, documentation).
  • Schedule patient appointments for Connected Care Center clinical services through various sources, including inbound calls, workqueues, clinical service requests, etc.
  • Act as a liaison and information resource for physicians and nursing support staff.
  • Return phone messages and send out new patient information packets via mail.
  • Direct patients to the appropriate clinicians for healthcare issues.
  • Process and route direct referrals to other clinical services.
  • Accurately enter patient information into the Epic system.
  • Utilize proper OHSU forms and documentation for all patients.
  • Collaborate with providers to maintain up-to-date clinic templates and block schedules in Epic.
  • Assist with scheduling surgical services as needed.

Registration, Managed Care, Financial Clearance

  • Ensure administrative and financial preparation of patients prior to their visit by following registration workflows. Gather and verify patient information, including demographics, insurance coverage, and financial status.
  • Pre-register patients with accurate demographic data, including race, ethnicity, language, and disability information.
  • Conduct financial screening using the Experian tool to determine patient eligibility for financial assistance programs.
  • Transfer patients to the appropriate department to address their financial concerns.
  • Confirm patient eligibility for healthcare coverage and clarify managed care arrangements.
  • Enter all information accurately into Epic EMR.
  • Set up reservations and admissions for elective inpatient and day patient procedures.
  • Obtain managed care authorizations for consultations, procedures, office visits, and care arrangements when needed. Follow up on pending authorizations until they are obtained.
  • Stay updated on managed care insurance plans and serve as a resource for physicians, nursing support staff, and colleagues.
  • Provide information on authorization requirements per diagnosis and service to referring physician offices, OHSU Health Plan Office, patients, and insurance companies.
  • Maintain proficiency in ICD-10 requirements.
  • Schedule appointments and coordinate with other ancillary and clinical services as necessary.
  • Resolve patient concerns and managed care-related problems using problem-solving and negotiation skills.
  • Create medical record if not already available.

Visit Preparation & Integrated Care

  • Prepare for patient visits by reviewing established visit preparation items and documenting their completion while speaking with the patient.
  • Contact referring providers to obtain any necessary items that have not been obtained.
  • Record, track, and verify referrals and authorizations for outpatient clinic and lab visits when required.
  • Schedule patient appointments and accommodate walk-ins as needed.
  • Obtain prior medical records and studies when necessary.
  • Arrange for stretchers, wheelchairs, interpreters, and other special accommodations as needed.
  • Send out information packets to patients.
  • Provide personal reminders to patients about upcoming appointments.
  • Prepare patient for virtual visits as needed

Referral Management:

  • Process incoming referrals for the Connected Care Center clinical services.
  • Verify and update patient demographics, including address, contact numbers, and primary care physician (PCP) information.
  • Ensure referrals contain the minimum required information.
  • Contact the referring clinic (internal or external) if any of the minimum required information is missing.
  • Utilize Media Manager software in Epic to upload documents into patient charts for current medical care or referral purposes.
  • Perform document scanning at the point of care, paying meticulous attention to detail to ensure accurate placement of records in the patient's chart.

Training and Competency

  • Engage in relevant educational activities to enhance knowledge and skills for assigned work.
  • Attend staff meetings, informational sessions, and other learning opportunities.
  • Stay up to date by reading vendor documentation, trade and other relevant publications.
  • Collaborate with peers and colleagues to exchange information.
  • Successfully complete required initial training and core competency assessment for PAS (Patient Access Services).
  • Stay up to date with all required OHSU and role specific modules.
  • Maintain core competencies and consistently apply acquired skills throughout employment.
  • Act as a resource for PAS expertise and share PAS information with other PAS Specialists in the service area.
  • Provide instruction to co-workers on user skills for PAS system software, including Order Entry, EPIC cadence scheduling, and the Radiology Information System (RIS).
  • Possess a working knowledge of diagnostic and procedural coding, medical terminology, and maintain familiarity with service-specific practices.
  • Fill in as needed for any PAS/R position within the service area.

Other Duties as Assigned

  • Including, but not limited to the following responsibilities:
  • Teamwork and Collaboration: Participates with team members in daily huddle discussing daily work for the team to align with OHSU service standards. Must have strong communication, listening skills and awareness of self. Collaborate with various teams to ensure patient access to care.

Required Qualifications

  • One year of experience in a medical office setting, including high-volume direct patient contact, scheduling of appointments and may require experience obtaining managed care authorizations (dependent on position description). OR one and a half years of work experience in a high volume direct public contact position and 6 months experience in a medical office setting. The candidate must have a thorough knowledge of PAS policies and procedures. Candidates will have demonstrated advanced PAS user skills as well as extensive knowledge of integrated care at OHSU.

Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • Basic computer skills including word processing. Windows applications, on-line scheduling, and a preference for data-base skills. Excellent verbal and written communications skills. Strong customer service orientation. Demonstrated effectiveness in confrontational customer interactions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced Degree

EmployeeAt Ensono, our Purpose is to be a relentless ally, disrupting the status quo and unleashing our clients to Do Great Things! We enable our clients to achieve key business outcomes that reshape how our world runs. As an expert technology adviser and managed service provider with cross-platform certifications, Ensono empowers our clients to keep up with continuous change and embrace innovation.

We can Do Great Things because we have great Associates. The Ensono Core Values unify our diverse talents and are woven into how we do business. These five traits are the key to achieving our purpose.

HONESTY, RELIABILITY, COLLABORATION, CURIOSITY, PASSION

Position Summary

Ensono’s Senior Technology Consultants are seasoned technologists focused on pushing forward technical innovation and transformation within the solution sets we provide. They work closely with our clients to understand their business drivers and objectives. Through collaboration with internal technologists, Senior Technology Consultants create solutions that drive value for our clients. They also provide client and industry feedback to Ensono’s internal teams, which allows Ensono to adjust our product and technology roadmaps. And finally, they are the lead architects delivering complex projects and programs for our clients.

The Senior Technology Consultant works alongside and supports Sales, Consulting and Client Success organizations to service our clients. They work with the clients’ business and technical teams to create reference architecture frameworks and templates. They lead the effort to execute multi-year transformation initiatives. To that end, Senior Technology Consultant must be effective in fostering executive level relationships with an emphasis on client satisfaction. Throughout the engagement process, from discovery to solution implementation, a Senior Technology Consultant must work with and at times lead multi-disciplinary teams. Other Qualifications

  • Advanced presentation & communication skills

  • Strong empathy, self-awareness, and interpersonal skills
